name: ChebyMap
note: The C class and astChebyMap headers write the recurrence as Tn+1 = 2x Tn + Tn-1; the code subtracts Tn-1, as the port's doc says (docs/issues/c-library-quirks.md)

name: astChebyDomain
note: C keeps no forward box when there are no forward coefficients and finds the forward domain by MapBox; the port always keeps the forward box given at creation (CH-8, docs/audits/mapping-c-parity.md; PLAN.md §2 row for that audit)

name: astChebyMap
note: C reads lbnd_i/ubnd_i whenever inverse coefficients are given and dereferences a NULL; the port refuses the call with Badin. C ignores lbnd_f/ubnd_f when there are no forward coefficients; the port requires them and keeps a forward box (CH-8, docs/audits/mapping-c-parity.md; PLAN.md §2 row for that audit)

name: astCmpMap
note: C keeps references to the components; the port's CmpMap takes ownership of them

name: DssMap
note: The header says a DSS FitsChan read creates a DssMap; C's FitsChan builds a TPN WcsMap instead, as the port does (docs/issues/c-library-quirks.md)

name: Frame
note: A plain Frame does not implement Mapping, where C's Frame is a unit Mapping with Nin = Nout = Naxes (PLAN.md 9.6: a bare Frame in a Mapping slot is not supported)

name: astAxAngle
note: C's header gives -PI/2 to +PI/2 for a 2-D Frame; the code returns astAngle's -PI to +PI, as the port's doc says (docs/issues/c-library-quirks.md)

name: astAxNorm
note: C's header says SkyFrame latitudes always go into -PI to +PI; a SkyFrame's own SkyAxes are not latitude axes in C's code, and the port mirrors that (docs/issues/c-library-quirks.md)

name: astConvert
note: C sets the Base of a FrameSet argument to the Frame used for the conversion; the port takes both by shared reference and leaves them unchanged (PLAN.md 2)

name: astFindFrame
note: C sets the Current of a FrameSet target to the Frame matched; the port leaves it unchanged (PLAN.md 2). The header's preference for paths with both transformations in a FrameSet search is not in C's FindFrame code, which takes the first match (docs/issues/c-library-quirks.md)

name: astNormPoints
note: Takes a PointSet, so no 8-byte variant or dimension arguments. C's public function reports AST__DIMIN for a coordinate count that differs from Naxes; the port reports Ncpin, as C's protected astNormalPoints does (PLAN.md 2)

name: astSetActiveUnit
note: C's header says a CmpFrame defaults to active units when both components use them, and that units with no Mapping between them raise an error; C's code uses either component, and treats such units as no match, as the port does (docs/issues/c-library-quirks.md)

name: astFrame
note: Attributes are set with the builder's typed methods rather than an options string

name: astPickAxes
note: For a Region, regions::pick_axes_region keeps the bounds where C's astPickAxes does

name: GrismNR
note: C refuses to set it on a GrismMap with more than one reference; owned values have no such restriction

name: GrismNRP
note: C refuses to set it on a GrismMap with more than one reference

name: GrismWaveR
note: C refuses to set it on a GrismMap with more than one reference

name: GrismAlpha
note: C refuses to set it on a GrismMap with more than one reference

name: GrismG
note: C refuses to set it on a GrismMap with more than one reference

name: GrismM
note: C refuses to set it on a GrismMap with more than one reference; the unset sentinel is INT_MAX, which set_grism_m(i32::MAX) mirrors

name: GrismEps
note: C refuses to set it on a GrismMap with more than one reference

name: GrismTheta
note: C refuses to set it on a GrismMap with more than one reference

name: astGrismMap
note: C takes only an options string; new sets every attribute and default_map sets none

name: IntraMap
note: The transformation is an Arc<dyn IntraTransform> held by the IntraMap; registration is needed only to read a dump

name: astIntraReg
note: C keeps one process-wide table; the port's registry belongs to the Channel that reads (Channel::register_intra), and an IntraMap made in code needs none. The name, numbers of coordinates, flags, purpose, author and contact are IntraTransform methods. C accepts a repeat registration whose arguments are all identical; the port accepts a repeat of the same Arc

name: IntraFlag
note: The header gives an empty-string default; the getter returns None while unset, and the merge compares an unset value as an empty string, as C does

name: astIntraMap
note: Takes the transformation itself rather than its registered name

name: LutInterp
note: C takes an integer (0 linear, otherwise nearest) and refuses a change on a LutMap with more than one reference; the port takes the LutInterp enum and owned values have no shared references

name: LutEpsilon
note: C refuses a change on a LutMap with more than one reference; owned values have no shared references

name: Mapping
note: rustdoc rejects an alias equal to the item's name, so the gate checks the trait's declaration

name: astLinearApprox
note: C's header says an all-bad box gives unit-transformation coefficients with bad offsets; C's code returns all-bad coefficients and zero, which the port returns as None

name: astRebin<X>
note: one function generic over RebinValue for the type codes

name: astRebinSeq<X>
note: one function generic over RebinValue for the type codes

name: astRemoveRegions
note: a Region becomes a UnitMap rather than its Frame, since the port's Frames are not Mappings (PLAN.md §9.6)

name: astResample<X>
note: ResampleFlags has no AST__URESAMP1-4 user flags (PLAN.md §2)

name: astSimplify
note: C returns the Mapping unsimplified when a reduction raises AST__NODEF or AST__TRNND; the port returns the error (PLAN.md §2)

name: astTranN
note: transform does not honor Report, which astTranN does (PLAN.md §2)

name: astTranP
note: transform_into does not honor Report, which astTranP does (PLAN.md §2)

name: astUinterp
note: no AST__URESAMP1-4 user flags reach it (see astResample<X>)

name: astUkern1
note: no AST__URESAMP1-4 user flags reach it (see astResample<X>)

name: Report
note: a clone keeps Report where C's copy clears it, and only tran1/tran2 report (PLAN.md §2); C's header says a dump drops it, but C's Dump writes it when set, as the port does

name: astDecompose
note: CmpMap and TranMap components are crate-private; CmpFrame::frame1/frame2 cover a CmpFrame (PLAN.md §2)

name: MathMap
note: The expression syntax from the astMathMap header is on the struct doc

name: astMathMap
note: C validates every variable name (AST__MISVN, AST__VARIN, AST__DUVAR); the port does not (PLAN.md §2). For nout < 1 C's final status is AST__BADNI (its second astError uses that code); the port returns Badno (docs/issues/c-library-quirks.md)

name: astMatrixMap
note: form 0 is new, form 1 is diagonal, and form 2 (unit) is diagonal with every element 1.0

name: astNormMap
note: The NormMap owns its Frame

name: Disco
note: C refuses to set it on a PcdMap with more than one reference; owned values have no such restriction

name: PcdCen
note: The getter returns both axes; C's PcdCen without an axis reads axis 1. C refuses to set it on a PcdMap with more than one reference

name: astPcdMap
note: The options string is replaced by the typed setters

name: astPermMap
note: C accepts a NULL inperm or outperm for the null permutation, dumped as InCpy/OutCpy; the port needs explicit arrays, which transform the same but dump every element (PLAN.md §2)

name: astPolyCoeffs
note: C also applies to a ChebyMap; ChebyMap has no coeffs and gives only the uninverted forward_terms/inverse_terms (PLAN.md §2)

name: astPolyTran
note: ChebyMap's Applicability text (NULL bounds use the ChebyMap's own box, Chebyshev result) is on ChebyMap::poly_tran

name: IterInverse
note: ChebyMap's Applicability (always zero, setting has no effect) is on the ChebyMap struct doc: ChebyMap has no iter_inverse methods

name: astPolyMap
note: C takes powers as doubles rounded to the nearest integer and rejects negative ones; the port takes PolyTerm with usize powers

name: astRateMap
note: The RateMap owns the encapsulated Mapping; C keeps a reference to it

name: astSelectorMap
note: badval is the builder's badval method, defaulting to BAD_VALUE

name: astSlaAdd
note: C takes the conversion as a string; the port takes SlaCvtType, whose variants carry the conversion list and SlaCvtType::from_code parses the strings

name: astSlaMap
note: C's reserved flags argument is dropped

name: astSpecAdd
note: C takes the conversion as a string; the port takes SpecCvtType, whose variants carry the conversion list and SpecCvtType::from_code parses the strings

name: astSpecMap
note: new is nin = 1; C's reserved flags argument is dropped

name: UnitRadius
note: C refuses to set it on a SphMap with more than one reference; owned values have no such restriction

name: PolarLong
note: C refuses to set it on a SphMap with more than one reference

name: astSphMap
note: The header says a zero vector transforms to AST__BAD; C's code (and the port) give (0, 0) from palDcc2s (docs/issues/c-library-quirks.md)

name: astSplineCoeffs
note: Returns a Vec of nx*ny values; C's nel argument (truncate or zero-fill) has no equivalent

name: astSplineKnots
note: One method per input axis in place of C's axis argument; C's nel argument (truncate or zero-fill) has no equivalent

name: InvNiter
note: The header's note that OutUnit changes the value returned for a non-converged point is dropped: C sets such points to AST__BAD whatever OutUnit is (splinemap.c:1595-1610), as the port does

name: astSplineMap
note: from_scipy takes C's SciPy coefficient order; new takes the X-fastest order of C's Fortran API and the dump. The port also checks the array lengths C takes on trust

name: astSwitchMap
note: The SwitchMap owns its components; C keeps references to them

name: astTimeAdd
note: C takes the conversion as a string; the port takes TimeCvtType, whose variants carry the conversion list and TimeCvtType::from_code parses the strings; the C header describes LASTTOLMST and LMSTTOLAST as GMST/LMST conversions, the port documents what they do (docs/issues/c-library-quirks.md)

name: astTimeMap
note: C's reserved flags argument is dropped

name: astTranMap
note: The TranMap owns its components; C keeps references to them

name: astUnitNormMap
note: ncoord is the length of the centre slice; C's undocumented NULL centre is equivalent to BAD_VALUE on every axis

name: ProjP
note: PVi_m

name: PVi_m
note: C refuses a change on a WcsMap with more than one reference; owned values have no shared references; the header's zero default for parameters the projection does not use holds only on the latitude axis, in C as in the port (wcsmap.c GetPV)

name: PVMax
note: C returns -1 for an axis that is neither longitude nor latitude; the port returns None

name: WcsAxis
note: WcsAxis(1) is lonax, WcsAxis(2) latax

name: astWcsMap
note: C sets projection parameters through the options string; the port sets them with set_pv after construction

name: Zoom
note: C forbids setting or clearing Zoom on a ZoomMap with more than one reference; the port has owned values, so set_zoom and clear_zoom always apply
